record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: How does Seiberg duality between brane tilings act on the associated dessins d’enfants, and can their duality trees suggest nontrivial Galois invariants?

evidence.quote: Question 28. How does Seiberg duality between brane tilings relate dessins d’enfants, and what Galois invariants (if any) can be inspired by these duality trees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A brane tiling is a bipartite graph drawn on a 2-torus that encodes the data (quiver with superpotential) of a four-dimensional N=1 supersymmetric gauge theory whose vacuum moduli space is a toric Calabi–Yau threefold. Seiberg duality acts on such gauge theories by a local move (urban renewal / square move on the bipartite graph) and produces, on the level of brane tilings, a tree (the duality tree) of dual phases. A dessin d'enfant is a connected bipartite graph embedded in a compact Riemann surface together with a Belyi map to ℙ¹ ramified only over {0,1,∞}; brane tilings on the torus, viewed as bipartite graphs with a complex structure, can be associated with dessins d'enfants in this way. The absolute Galois group Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) acts faithfully on the set of dessins, partitioning them into Galois orbits, and a Galois invariant is any function of a dessin that is constant on each orbit (e.g. the passport, the monodromy group, the field of moduli).

Problem. (a) Determine precisely how Seiberg duality between brane tilings (the urban renewal/square move and its iterations) acts on the associated dessins d'enfants: identify the induced transformation on the corresponding Belyi pair (X,β) (or, when the dessin lives on a higher genus curve, on the associated bipartite map) and describe its effect on standard Galois-theoretic data (passport, monodromy, field of moduli, etc.).

(b) Using the structure of Seiberg duality trees (the trees of dual phases of a fixed toric Calabi–Yau threefold), construct nontrivial Galois invariants of dessins d'enfants — i.e. functions of the dessin that (i) are demonstrably constant on Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)-orbits and (ii) are not implied by the standard known Galois invariants — or prove that no such new invariants arise from this construction.
artifact.status_search_result: Related literature establishes partial results: the degree of the number field of definition and the confinement index have been identified as Seiberg duality / Galois invariants, and brane tilings beyond the torus have been linked to dessins. However, no work appears to give a complete description of how Seiberg duality acts on the associated dessins or to derive new Galois invariants from duality trees in the sense asked. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Invariants of Toric Seiberg Duality
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies invariants under toric Seiberg duality, including number-theoretic invariants of the associated Belyi data.
status_evidence.claim: Some Seiberg duality invariants (e.g. degree of field extension) are known, but a full characterization of the action on dessins is not given.

status_evidence.title: Gauge theories and dessins d'enfants: beyond the torus
status_evidence.snippet: Extends the dessins d'enfants/brane tiling correspondence beyond the torus.
status_evidence.claim: Provides framework but does not resolve how Seiberg duality acts on dessins or produce new Galois invariants from duality trees.

status_evidence.title: Machine-Learning Dessins d'Enfants
status_evidence.snippet: Explores dessins via machine learning, suggesting the classification problem is still being investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates the problem of identifying Galois invariants of brane-tiling dessins is an active, unresolved area.
